question:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite directed acyclic graph with |E| > 0. Which of the following must be true?
I. G has a vertex with no incoming edge.
II. G has a vertex with no outgoing edge.
III. G has an isolated vertex, that is, one with neither an incoming edge nor an outgoing edge.
options: I and III only
None of the above
I and II only
II and III only
I, II, and a vertex with one outgoing edge
I, II, and a vertex with one incoming edge
All of the above (I, II, III)
II only
I only
III only
model_outputs:
A directed acyclic graph (DAG) is a graph with no cycles. In a DAG, every edge points from a vertex to another vertex, and there cannot be any loops (edges that point back to a vertex).
I. A vertex with no incoming edges (in-degree 0) is possible in a DAG. This vertex is a sink, and such vertices do exist. So this statement is true.

II. A vertex with no outgoing edges (out-degree 0) is also possible in a DAG. This vertex is a source, and such vertices do exist. So this statement is true.

III. An isolated vertex is a vertex with neither an incoming nor an outgoing edge. In a DAG, since all edges point from one vertex to another, there cannot be a vertex with neither an incoming nor an outgoing edge. Therefore, this statement is false.

Therefore, I and II are true, but III is false. The answer is (C).
